title: Real-Time Bidding (RTB), CTR Calibration & Bid Shading

spark.summary: Real-Time Bidding (RTB) & CTR Calibration converts raw neural click probabilities into profitable first-price auction bids within a strict 100ms OpenRTB round-trip.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a user loads a webpage, the SSP/Ad Exchange broadcasts an OpenRTB JSON/Protobuf BidRequest with tmax=100ms, in first-price auctions, an uncalibrated CTR model or naive expected-value bid overpays dramatically; you must calibrate pCTR (Isotonic/Platt) and apply bid shading.
spark.byteSummary:
In programmatic advertising, every page load triggers an OpenRTB auction where DSPs have under 100ms (often 30–50ms internal compute) to evaluate an ad slot and return a dollar bid.

Because deep CTR models (DCNv2/DeepFM) trained with negative downsampling output uncalibrated log-odds, raw scores must pass through Isotonic Regression or Platt Scaling to recover true calibrated probabilities (pCTR). Expected value is then eCPM = pCTR * CPC * 1000.

Under modern first-price auctions, bidding full expected value yields zero surplus. Bid shading models predict the minimum winning price distribution to shade the bid down while preserving win rate, and delayed click/conversion feedback updates FTRL-Proximal online weights.

learningJourney.title: Expected Value & Negative Downsampling Correction
learningJourney.purpose: Convert downsampled model outputs into true calibrated click probabilities.

explanation.core: To speed up training, negative (non-click) impressions are downsampled by rate w (e.g., 0.1).
explanation.deepDive: Without recalibrating p_true = p_model / (p_model + (1 - p_model) / w), predicted CTR is inflated by ~10x, causing massive overspending.

cards.label: Isotonic Calibration
cards.detail: Non-parametric isotonic regression fixes non-linear neural score distortion.

sectionDiagram.summary: Log-odds prior correction and isotonic calibration turn neural scores into true probabilities.
sectionDiagram.caption: Accurate eCPM valuation depends on calibrated probabilities, not just AUC ranking.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Real-Time Bidding (RTB), CTR Calibration & Bid Shading without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When a user loads a webpage, the SSP/Ad Exchange broadcasts an OpenRTB JSON/Protobuf BidRequest with tmax=100ms, in first-price auctions, an uncalibrated CTR model or naive expected-value bid overpays dramatically; you must calibrate pCTR (Isotonic/Platt) and apply bid shading.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: First-Price Auctions & Bid Shading
learningJourney.purpose: Maximize advertiser ROI by bidding just above the expected clearing price.

explanation.foundation: In second-price auctions, bidding true value v was optimal.
explanation.core: In modern first-price auctions, you pay what you bid.
explanation.deepDive: Bid Shading models estimate the clearing-price CDF P(win | bid) and choose b* = argmax (v - b) * P(win | b), typically saving 15%–30% of media spend.

learningJourney.title: Delayed Attribution & Streaming Joiners
learningJourney.purpose: Join bid requests, win notices, impressions, and delayed clicks in Flink.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Delayed Attribution & Streaming Joiners** as the intuition layer for Real-Time Bidding (RTB), CTR Calibration & Bid Shading: Join bid requests, win notices, impressions, and delayed clicks in Flink.
explanation.core: A bid request occurs at t=0, win notice at t=50ms, impression pixel at t=500ms, and click at t=10s–24h. Flink maintains a RocksDB interval-join keyed by auction_id across a 2-hour window, emitting negative samples on timeout and positive samples on click.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, delayed attribution & streaming joiners becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. learningJourney.title: FTRL-Proximal Online Learning
learningJourney.purpose: Update sparse ad-ID and publisher-ID weights in real time within minutes.

explanation.foundation: Think of **FTRL-Proximal Online Learning** as the intuition layer for Real-Time Bidding (RTB), CTR Calibration & Bid Shading: Update sparse ad-ID and publisher-ID weights in real time within minutes.
explanation.core: New ad creatives launch constantly and need rapid CTR adaptation. FTRL-Proximal (Follow-The-Regularized-Leader) with L1+L2 regularization updates sparse embedding tables online via Parameter Servers, driving irrelevant feature weights to exact zero for compact memory.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, ftrl-proximal online learning becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production RTB theory covering Flink interval-joined delayed attribution, FTRL-Proximal sparse online updates, and pre-training IVT scrubbing.

learningJourney.codeExample:
def ftrl_update(z, n, g, alpha=0.05, beta=1.0, l1=1.0, l2=1.0):
    sigma = (math.sqrt(n + g * g) - math.sqrt(n)) / alpha
    z_new = z + g - sigma * 0.0  # simplified weight w
    n_new = n + g * g
    return z_new, n_new

learningJourney.title: Click Fraud & Invalid Traffic (IVT) Filtering
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent bots and click-farms from draining advertiser budgets and poisoning CTR models.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Click Fraud & Invalid Traffic (IVT) Filtering** as the intuition layer for Real-Time Bidding (RTB), CTR Calibration & Bid Shading: Prevent bots and click-farms from draining advertiser budgets and poisoning CTR models.
explanation.core: Botnets generate fake clicks that distort both billing and online learning gradients. A streaming IVT detector flags headless browsers, datacenter ASN bursts, and sub-100ms click-after-impression anomalies before clicks enter billing or FTRL training.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, click fraud & invalid traffic (ivt) filtering becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. knowledgeChecks.question: You train a DeepFM CTR model with 10% negative downsampling (w=0.1) and deploy it directly to a first-price auction without recalibration. What happens?

options.text: Predicted CTRs are inflated by ~10x, causing massive overbidding and budget burn
options.feedback: Correct! You must apply log-odds prior correction p_true = p / (p + (1-p)/w) before computing eCPM.

options.text: Predicted CTRs drop to zero and the DSP never bids
options.feedback: Downsampling negatives increases the apparent positive ratio, inflating pCTR rather than shrinking it.

options.text: OpenRTB tmax timeouts drop from 100ms to 10ms
options.feedback: Negative downsampling affects probability calibration, not network tmax.
FTRL continues updating, though gradients would also be miscalibrated.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Negative downsampling shifts the base rate; log-odds correction restores true calibrated probabilities.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is Bid Shading critical in modern first-price programmatic ad auctions?

options.text: It encrypts user PII inside OpenRTB requests
options.feedback: Bid shading is a pricing optimization, not an encryption mechanism.

options.text: It lowers bids toward the predicted clearing price to preserve advertiser surplus instead of paying full expected value
options.feedback: Correct! In first-price auctions you pay your bid, so shading saves 15-30% spend while maintaining win rates.

options.text: It eliminates the need for Redis budget pacing
options.feedback: Budget pacing is still required to spread daily spend across 24 hours.

options.text: It forces all SSPs to switch back to second-price auctions
options.feedback: DSPs cannot dictate exchange auction rules.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: First-price auctions charge the exact winning bid, making bid shading essential for positive ROI.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should Invalid Traffic (IVT) and bot-click filtering run BEFORE the FTRL-Proximal online learning pipeline?

options.text: To reduce Redis Cluster memory usage for Aerospike
options.feedback: Aerospike and Redis are separate stores; IVT filtering is about signal integrity.

options.text: To speed up TensorRT FP16 kernel compilation
options.feedback: Kernel compilation is offline and unrelated to click streams.

options.text: To prevent the CTR model from learning to bid aggressively on bot-heavy inventory
options.feedback: Correct! Training on unverified bot clicks causes the model to chase fraudulent high-CTR placements.

options.text: To increase OpenRTB tmax from 100ms to 500ms
options.feedback: IVT filtering runs asynchronously on click streams, not during the synchronous bid.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Training on unfiltered bot clicks poisons online gradients and wastes ad spend on non-human traffic.
